Intangible Asset — Amortization

This screen displays all accumulated amortization transactions for a specific intangible asset.

Amortization is the process of systematically allocating the cost of an intangible asset over its useful life, similar to how depreciation works for fixed assets.

Understanding the Transactions

The transactions shown here represent the periodic amortization entries that have been recorded for this intangible asset.

Each entry increases the accumulated amortization balance, which in turn reduces the net book value of the intangible asset.

These entries are typically created through amortization entries or journal entries that affect the intangible asset's accumulated amortization account.

Reading the Information

The running balance column shows the total accumulated amortization at any point in time.

You can use this information to track how much of the intangible asset's cost has been amortized and how much remains to be amortized over its remaining useful life.
